newsitem.title: CHILE: Telex-Chile in deal with Qualcomm.
newsitem.headline: Telex-Chile in deal with Qualcomm.

text.p: Telex-Chile SA said it has sold 50 percent of its mobile telephone unit Chilesat PCS to U.S. telecom Qualcomm Inc for $42 million.
"Qualcomm...made a capital contribution of $42 million in cash to Chilesat PCS in exchange for a share of 50 percent in the company," said the statement.
Telex said it will use Qualcomm's CDMA technology to build a national PCS personal telephone network.
Telex has also signed a $90 million supply contract with the U.S. firm to intall a network and terminals which will be financed by a long-term loan from Qualcomm.
Chilesat PCS plans to invest $300 million over the next five years to set a mobile telephone network to supply some 300,000 customers, said the statement.
The company was awarded one of three PCS licences issued last year and will start operating the service in April when the authorization is granted officially.
Telex has long been looking for an alliance with a heavyweight foreign partner to help it compete in Chile's deregulated long-distance telecom market.
Until this deal was signed, it was the only large local company not to have linked up with a foreign player.

Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile, the country's largest carrier, is some 43-percent owned by Spain's Telefonica de Espana. Italian firm Stet SpA bought 16 percent of Entel Chile SA last year for $273 million.
